**1 — Scene:** An assorted maki sushi meal with pickled ginger, wasabi, and soy sauce. I’m treating the central sushi plate as the target; the spring rolls and salad on separate plates are excluded.

**2 — Vessel:** The sushi plate appears to be about **22 cm** across: area ≈ 3.14 × 11² = **380 cm²**. The condiments are in small cups beside it.

**3 — Items:** Eight maki pieces containing rice, seaweed, and mixed fish/vegetable fillings; pickled ginger; wasabi; soy sauce.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Area coverage | Gross volume calculation | Density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Assorted maki, 8 pieces | 28% of plate = 106 cm² | 106 × 2.5 cm = 265 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 212 g | 155 | 329 kcal |
| Pickled ginger | ~70% of a 4 cm cup = 9 cm² | 9 × 1.8 cm = 16 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 10 g | 60 | 6 kcal |
| Wasabi | ~25% of a 4 cm cup = 3 cm² | 3 × 1 cm = 3 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 3 g | 110 | 3 kcal |
| Soy sauce | ~90% of a 4 cm cup = 11 cm² | 11 × 1.4 cm = 15 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 15 g | 55 | 8 kcal |

The sushi covers approximately **28% of its plate**, with the rest exposed. Condiment coverage is calculated separately within each cup, not added to the plate coverage.

**8 — Sanity check:** About 26 g per maki piece is plausible for the visible size. Including condiments, the estimate is **240 g and 346 kcal**. Filling composition is the main energy uncertainty.
